**RE: Appeal of Adverse Benefit Determination — Knee Arthroscopy / Meniscus Surgery (CPT 29881)**

- **Member name:** Skyler Brooks
- **Member ID:** W379841926
- **Reference number:** POC-9F671E8F0E-86300
- **Date of denial notice:** 2026-08-07
- **Plan / product:** Wellpoint (Amerigroup), Commercial/ACA, Tennessee
- **Governing policy:** Carelon Joint Surgery (MSK02-1125.1), https://guidelines.carelonmedicalbenefitsmanagement.com/joint-surgery-2025-11-15/

---

Dear Appeals Reviewer,

I am appealing the denial of prior authorization for the knee arthroscopy with partial meniscectomy (CPT 29881) requested by my orthopedic surgeon, Dr. Okafor. I am asking the plan to reconsider that decision and approve the surgery.

The notice dated 2026-08-07 states that the records submitted do not document an adequate trial of conservative treatment before surgery. I am writing because the plan's own published criteria describe the conservative care that is required, and my medical records document that care. Below I quote the plan's policy language and point to the records that match it.

---

## The plan's criteria, and what my records show

**1. The conservative-care requirement in the policy**

The Carelon Joint Surgery policy states that surgery is medically necessary for a chronic degenerative meniscal tear "when ALL the following are present:" and lists, among them:

> "Persistent or frequent mechanical symptoms (catching, locking, or instability) or failure of conservative management for at least 12 weeks"

My records establish both parts of that alternative, either of which the policy states is sufficient:

- **Conservative management longer than 12 weeks.** I completed supervised physical therapy focused on quadriceps strengthening and range of motion for 16 weeks, from 2026-03-04 to 2026-06-24, with 18 visits completed. This is documented in my physical therapy discharge note.
- **Persistent mechanical symptoms.** My records document locking and giving way. I cannot squat or kneel, and I am limited to level walking.

**2. The policy's description of what conservative care must include**

The policy states that conservative management:

> "must include a combination of strategies to reduce inflammation, alleviate pain, and correct underlying dysfunction, including physical therapy AND at least ONE complementary conservative treatment strategy"

My records document physical therapy plus more than one complementary treatment: NSAIDs for 4 months with inadequate relief, and a corticosteroid injection on 2026-05-04 that gave only about two weeks of partial relief.

**3. The policy's documentation requirement**

The policy states:

> "Documentation of compliance with a plan of therapy that includes elements from these areas is required where conservative management is appropriate."

My compliance is documented: 18 completed physical therapy visits over 16 weeks, recorded in the physical therapy discharge note, along with the medication trial and the injection date. If the physical therapy discharge note was not part of the file the reviewer saw, I am asking that it be obtained and reviewed, and I am requesting reconsideration on that basis.

**4. Imaging**

The policy states:

> "The provider shall submit a detailed imaging report for studies obtained within the past 12 months that correlates with clinical findings of the requested procedure."

and

> "Imaging demonstrating a meniscal tear consistent with the clinical presentation"

My MRI of the knee was obtained on 2026-07-10, within the past 12 months. It shows a displaced bucket-handle tear of the medial meniscus with mechanical locking. That finding matches my symptoms exactly: my records document locking and giving way.

**5. Arthritis severity**

The policy states:

> "Imaging findings demonstrate no more than moderate osteoarthritis as evidenced by imaging showing ONE of the following:"

and includes as one of those findings:

> "Kellgren-Lawrence grade ≤ 2"

My 2026-07-10 MRI reports articular cartilage preserved and Kellgren-Lawrence grade 1. That is within the range the policy identifies.

**6. Symptoms and examination**

The policy also lists:

> "Moderate to severe pain associated with functional limitation, which interferes with the ability to perform age-appropriate daily activities"

> "Symptoms of catching, locking, or instability"

> "Physical exam* consistent with meniscus pathology (e.g., Joint Line Tenderness, McMurray, Apley, effusion, reduced range of motion)"

My records document 14 months of progressive knee pain that is not relieved by rest; locking and giving way; inability to squat or kneel; walking limited to level surfaces; positive provocative testing on the affected side; and range of motion limited by pain.

**7. The procedure requested**

The policy states:

> "Partial meniscectomy is considered medically necessary for symptomatic tears not amenable to repair, especially when the peripheral meniscal rim is intact."

My surgeon, Dr. Okafor, has documented that this procedure is needed for my condition and requested CPT 29881. My records also note no active infection, no untreated substance use, BMI 29, and that I am a non-smoker.

---

## A note on the criteria applied

Several passages of the policy I have access to end in a colon and introduce lists of further conditions that were not reproduced in the excerpts available to me. I am not able to quote those additional items, and I am not assuming what they say. I am asking the plan to identify in writing the specific criterion or criteria from Carelon Joint Surgery (MSK02-1125.1) that my records were found not to meet, so that I can respond to the actual basis for the decision. I would also note that the denial notice states a conclusion about my conservative treatment but does not identify a required duration or number of visits, and I am not aware of a stated threshold in the policy language available to me beyond the 12-week alternative quoted above — which my 16 weeks of physical therapy exceeds.

---

## What I am asking for

I respectfully request that the plan:

1. Overturn the denial issued 2026-08-07 (reference POC-9F671E8F0E-86300) and authorize CPT 29881;
2. Have this appeal reviewed by a physician reviewer with orthopedic expertise;
3. Provide me, at no charge, a copy of the specific criteria and the clinical rationale used in the review, and identify which criterion my records were found not to satisfy; and
4. Consider the enclosed records, including my physical therapy discharge note, medication and injection records, the 2026-07-10 MRI report, and my surgeon's office notes.

I understand my appeal must be received within 180 days of the date of the notice, by **2027-02-03**, and I am submitting it within that period. I am sending this appeal to the address printed on my denial letter; I understand I can also submit or check on it at anthem.com, through the Sydney Health app, or by calling the number on the back of my ID card.

Thank you for taking the time to look at this again. I would like to get back to walking, kneeling, and daily activities without my knee locking, and my surgeon has documented that this procedure is what I need.

Sincerely,

**Skyler Brooks**
